title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page has nothing to do with motives. It is a typed Bourbaki document, 'Tribu n° 59', section 'ALGÈBRES de LIE SEMI-SIMPLES (8)'. It is filed upside down, which suggests Grothendieck used the reverse of an old Bourbaki circular as scrap paper; the neighbouring pages are his handwritten notes on motivic Galois theory and comparison of realizations. The text is a list of editorial instructions on a draft (état 8) of what became Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, ch. VIII.

The mathematics, in modern terms, for a split semisimple Lie algebra g with splitting Cartan subalgebra h and root system R:
(1) Prop. 2 (regular subalgebras). Every h-stable subspace V has the form V = h' ⊕ ⊕_{α∈Σ} g^α, with h' ⊂ h and Σ ⊂ R. V is a subalgebra iff Σ is closed and α ∈ Σ∩(−Σ) implies H_α ∈ h'.
(2) The radical of V should be exhibited explicitly. It is built from a part of h' and the g^α with α ∈ Σ, −α ∉ Σ.
(3) Prop. 3. V is reductive iff Σ is closed and symmetric. V is semisimple iff, in addition, h' is spanned by the H_α (α ∈ Σ). In that case its root system is Σ.
(4) Borel subalgebras. The Killing form vanishes on n^±. Their orthogonals are Borel subalgebras. Parabolic ('paraboréliques') subalgebras are to be discussed.
(5) n° 7 terminology. S becomes 'base de R' and is to be indexed. The Serre relations (ad X_i)^{−a_ij+1} X_j = (ad Y_i)^{−a_ij+1} Y_j = 0 are to be stated here. The triple (H_i, X_i, Y_i) should not get its own name; it is 'associated with the pinning' (épinglage).
(6) n° 8 (Chevalley basis / structure constants N_{αβ}). Specify X_α ∈ g^α, move a lemma, and introduce p into Prop. 6 (the root-string length). Explain that a formula holds because α+β is a root.

All of this matches published Bourbaki Lie ch. VIII, §3 (regular subalgebras, Borel and parabolic subalgebras) and §4 (pinnings, Serre relations, Chevalley bases).
errors: The orthogonals of n^+ and n^- under the Killing form are b^+ and b^- respectively. Read in order, the text pairs n^+ with b^- and n^- with b^+. This is a slip unless the pairing was not meant respectively. (n^+⊥ = h ⊕ n^+ = b^+, since B(g^α, g^β) = 0 unless α+β = 0 and B(h, g^α) = 0.)

ideas.what: Classification of h-stable subspaces and subalgebras via closed subsets of roots; criteria for reductive and semisimple regular subalgebras

deep.surprise_reason: This is a misfiled or reused Bourbaki editorial report on the Lie algebras draft, with no connection to the surrounding motivic notes. Its content is all in published Bourbaki ch. VIII. The only minor curiosities are the archival point that Grothendieck reused Bourbaki circulars as scrap paper, and the term 'paraboréliques'.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down; the transcription correctly reads it as Bourbaki 'Tribu n° 59', unrelated to the motivic notes on neighbouring pages.
'193' is the archive folio number written in the margin, not part of the text.
